005package org.wpilib.math.controller;
006
007import org.wpilib.math.controller.proto.ElevatorFeedforwardProto;
008import org.wpilib.math.controller.struct.ElevatorFeedforwardStruct;
009import org.wpilib.util.protobuf.ProtobufSerializable;
010import org.wpilib.util.struct.StructSerializable;
011
012/**
013 * A helper class that computes feedforward outputs for a simple elevator (modeled as a motor acting
014 * against the force of gravity).
015 */
016public class ElevatorFeedforward implements ProtobufSerializable, StructSerializable {
017  /** The static gain, in volts. */
018  private double ks;
019
020  /** The gravity gain, in volts. */
021  private double kg;
022
023  /** The velocity gain, in V/(m/s). */
024  private double kv;
025
026  /** The acceleration gain, in V/(m/s²). */
027  private double ka;
028
029  /** The period, in seconds. */
030  private final double m_dt;
031
032  /**
033   * Creates a new ElevatorFeedforward with the specified gains and period.
034   *
035   * @param ks The static gain in volts.
036   * @param kg The gravity gain in volts.
037   * @param kv The velocity gain in V/(m/s).
038   * @param ka The acceleration gain in V/(m/s²).
039   * @param dt The period in seconds.
040   * @throws IllegalArgumentException for kv &lt; zero.
041   * @throws IllegalArgumentException for ka &lt; zero.
042   * @throws IllegalArgumentException for period &le; zero.
043   */
044  public ElevatorFeedforward(double ks, double kg, double kv, double ka, double dt) {
045    this.ks = ks;
046    this.kg = kg;
047    this.kv = kv;
048    this.ka = ka;
049    if (kv < 0.0) {
050      throw new IllegalArgumentException("kv must be a non-negative number, got " + kv + "!");
051    }
052    if (ka < 0.0) {
053      throw new IllegalArgumentException("ka must be a non-negative number, got " + ka + "!");
054    }
055    if (dt <= 0.0) {
056      throw new IllegalArgumentException("period must be a positive number, got " + dt + "!");
057    }
058    m_dt = dt;
059  }
060
061  /**
062   * Creates a new ElevatorFeedforward with the specified gains. The period is defaulted to 20 ms.
063   *
064   * @param ks The static gain in volts.
065   * @param kg The gravity gain in volts.
066   * @param kv The velocity gain in V/(m/s).
067   * @param ka The acceleration gain in V/(m/s²).
068   * @throws IllegalArgumentException for kv &lt; zero.
069   * @throws IllegalArgumentException for ka &lt; zero.
070   */
071  public ElevatorFeedforward(double ks, double kg, double kv, double ka) {
072    this(ks, kg, kv, ka, 0.020);
073  }
074
075  /**
076   * Creates a new ElevatorFeedforward with the specified gains. Acceleration gain is defaulted to
077   * zero. The period is defaulted to 20 ms.
078   *
079   * @param ks The static gain in volts.
080   * @param kg The gravity gain in volts.
081   * @param kv The velocity gain in V/(m/s).
082   * @throws IllegalArgumentException for kv &lt; zero.
083   */
084  public ElevatorFeedforward(double ks, double kg, double kv) {
085    this(ks, kg, kv, 0);
086  }
087
088  /**
089   * Sets the static gain.
090   *
091   * <p>This setter is intended for online tuning only. Feedforward gains are assumed constant, so
092   * gain scheduling means the system was not correctly modeled.
093   *
094   * @param ks The static gain in volts.
095   */
096  public void setKs(double ks) {
097    this.ks = ks;
098  }
099
100  /**
101   * Sets the gravity gain.
102   *
103   * <p>This setter is intended for online tuning only. Feedforward gains are assumed constant, so
104   * gain scheduling means the system was not correctly modeled.
105   *
106   * @param kg The gravity gain in volts.
107   */
108  public void setKg(double kg) {
109    this.kg = kg;
110  }
111
112  /**
113   * Sets the velocity gain.
114   *
115   * <p>This setter is intended for online tuning only. Feedforward gains are assumed constant, so
116   * gain scheduling means the system was not correctly modeled.
117   *
118   * @param kv The velocity gain in V/(m/s).
119   */
120  public void setKv(double kv) {
121    this.kv = kv;
122  }
123
124  /**
125   * Sets the acceleration gain.
126   *
127   * <p>This setter is intended for online tuning only. Feedforward gains are assumed constant, so
128   * gain scheduling means the system was not correctly modeled.
129   *
130   * @param ka The acceleration gain in V/(m/s²).
131   */
132  public void setKa(double ka) {
133    this.ka = ka;
134  }
135
136  /**
137   * Returns the static gain in volts.
138   *
139   * @return The static gain in volts.
140   */
141  public double getKs() {
142    return ks;
143  }
144
145  /**
146   * Returns the gravity gain in volts.
147   *
148   * @return The gravity gain in volts.
149   */
150  public double getKg() {
151    return kg;
152  }
153
154  /**
155   * Returns the velocity gain in V/(m/s).
156   *
157   * @return The velocity gain.
158   */
159  public double getKv() {
160    return kv;
161  }
162
163  /**
164   * Returns the acceleration gain in V/(m/s²).
165   *
166   * @return The acceleration gain.
167   */
168  public double getKa() {
169    return ka;
170  }
171
172  /**
173   * Returns the period in seconds.
174   *
175   * @return The period in seconds.
176   */
177  public double getDt() {
178    return m_dt;
179  }
180
181  /**
182   * Calculates the feedforward from the gains and velocity reference assuming continuous control
183   * (acceleration is assumed to be zero).
184   *
185   * @param velocity The velocity reference in meters per second.
186   * @return The computed feedforward.
187   */
188  public double calculate(double velocity) {
189    return calculate(velocity, velocity);
190  }
191
192  /**
193   * Calculates the feedforward from the gains and references assuming discrete control.
194   *
195   * <p>Note this method is inaccurate when the velocity crosses 0.
196   *
197   * @param currentVelocity The current velocity reference in meters per second.
198   * @param nextVelocity The next velocity reference in meters per second.
199   * @return The computed feedforward.
200   */
201  public double calculate(double currentVelocity, double nextVelocity) {
202    // See wpimath/docs/ElevatorFeedforward.md for derivation
203    if (ka < 1e-9) {
204      return ks * Math.signum(nextVelocity) + kg + kv * nextVelocity;
205    } else {
206      double A = -kv / ka;
207      double B = 1.0 / ka;
208      double A_d = Math.exp(A * m_dt);
209      double B_d = A > -1e-9 ? B * m_dt : 1.0 / A * (A_d - 1.0) * B;
210      return kg
211          + ks * Math.signum(currentVelocity)
212          + 1.0 / B_d * (nextVelocity - A_d * currentVelocity);
213    }
214  }
215
216  // Rearranging the main equation from the calculate() method yields the
217  // formulas for the methods below:
218
219  /**
220   * Calculates the maximum achievable velocity given a maximum voltage supply and an acceleration.
221   * Useful for ensuring that velocity and acceleration constraints for a trapezoidal profile are
222   * simultaneously achievable - enter the acceleration constraint, and this will give you a
223   * simultaneously-achievable velocity constraint.
224   *
225   * @param maxVoltage The maximum voltage that can be supplied to the elevator, in volts.
226   * @param acceleration The acceleration of the elevator, in (m/s²).
227   * @return The maximum possible velocity in (m/s) at the given acceleration.
228   */
229  public double maxAchievableVelocity(double maxVoltage, double acceleration) {
230    // Assume max velocity is positive
231    return (maxVoltage - ks - kg - acceleration * ka) / kv;
232  }
233
234  /**
235   * Calculates the minimum achievable velocity given a maximum voltage supply and an acceleration.
236   * Useful for ensuring that velocity and acceleration constraints for a trapezoidal profile are
237   * simultaneously achievable - enter the acceleration constraint, and this will give you a
238   * simultaneously-achievable velocity constraint.
239   *
240   * @param maxVoltage The maximum voltage that can be supplied to the elevator, in volts.
241   * @param acceleration The acceleration of the elevator, in (m/s²).
242   * @return The maximum possible velocity in (m/s) at the given acceleration.
243   */
244  public double minAchievableVelocity(double maxVoltage, double acceleration) {
245    // Assume min velocity is negative, ks flips sign
246    return (-maxVoltage + ks - kg - acceleration * ka) / kv;
247  }
248
249  /**
250   * Calculates the maximum achievable acceleration given a maximum voltage supply and a velocity.
251   * Useful for ensuring that velocity and acceleration constraints for a trapezoidal profile are
252   * simultaneously achievable - enter the velocity constraint, and this will give you a
253   * simultaneously-achievable acceleration constraint.
254   *
255   * @param maxVoltage The maximum voltage that can be supplied to the elevator, in volts.
256   * @param velocity The velocity of the elevator, in (m/s)
257   * @return The maximum possible acceleration in (m/s²) at the given velocity.
258   */
259  public double maxAchievableAcceleration(double maxVoltage, double velocity) {
260    return (maxVoltage - ks * Math.signum(velocity) - kg - velocity * kv) / ka;
261  }
262
263  /**
264   * Calculates the minimum achievable acceleration given a maximum voltage supply and a velocity.
265   * Useful for ensuring that velocity and acceleration constraints for a trapezoidal profile are
266   * simultaneously achievable - enter the velocity constraint, and this will give you a
267   * simultaneously-achievable acceleration constraint.
268   *
269   * @param maxVoltage The maximum voltage that can be supplied to the elevator, in volts.
270   * @param velocity The velocity of the elevator, in (m/s)
271   * @return The maximum possible acceleration in (m/s²) at the given velocity.
272   */
273  public double minAchievableAcceleration(double maxVoltage, double velocity) {
274    return maxAchievableAcceleration(-maxVoltage, velocity);
275  }
276
277  /** ElevatorFeedforward struct for serialization. */
278  public static final ElevatorFeedforwardStruct struct = new ElevatorFeedforwardStruct();
279
280  /** ElevatorFeedforward protobuf for serialization. */
281  public static final ElevatorFeedforwardProto proto = new ElevatorFeedforwardProto();
282}
